The Wall Street Journal has revealed 🔰 Round-the-clock production cannot make up for America's weapons shortfall either 🔸The reputable American business and economic newspaper revealed that even 24-hour production by American military factories cannot compensate for the severe weapons shortage in the country brought about by the war against Iran. 🔸According to Foreign Affairs, the Pentagon, in order to counter this effective strategy of Iran, has depleted America's strategic missile reserves, such as Tomahawk, SM-6 missiles, and other expensive systems. As a result, Washington is now forced to rapidly replenish its own weapons stockpiles as well as those of its partners elsewhere, including Taiwan and Ukraine. 🔸Nevertheless, the Wall Street Journal has acknowledged that the efforts of military companies and defense contractors to produce advanced missiles to fill America's empty arsenal have not yielded any tangible results. This reputable business and economic newspaper states that "Defense companies are rushing to increase missile production. But it is too late." According to this report, America has fired more than 1,000 Tomahawk missiles in just two months of war with Iran. The country has also used up nearly half of its reserves of advanced Patriot interceptors and desperately needs to replace these weapons, and in a short time at that. 🔸The Wall Street Journal also believes that one of the root causes of this crisis in the United States' ammunition-manufacturing industries is that investment in missile production factories has been insufficient in recent years, and the contradictory and ever-changing contracts the Pentagon has signed with contractors have also dealt a blow to the sector. According to this publication, many of the key factories considered the backbone of supplying the American army's weapons have for years struggled with worn-out equipment and a shortage of skilled personnel. The Wall Street Journal goes on to write: Even if all production increase programs proceed according to plan, reaching the desired level of missile inventory will take at least two years. This means that in the short term, the American army will face a serious limitation in its offensive and defensive capabilities. #Foreign_Service https://kayhan.ir/001QB3 🔘 Bale | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram @Kayhan_Online

entry.title: [Kayhan_online] 🔰The missing arrow in the bow of sports management!🔸Gholamreza…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @Kayhan_online

🔰The missing arrow in the bow of sports management!🔸Gholamreza Shabani-Bahar, head of the Archery Federation, went on Radio Varzesh yesterday after the recurve competitions at the 2026 Asian Games to discuss the problems and costs of this discipline—a discipline that is equipment-driven and involves specialized gear with specific, calculable costs.🔸But what stood out more than archery's problems in this roughly 10-minute conversation was the bizarre muddle in stating the simplest numbers and figures. When the talk turned to the price of an arrow, the numbers kept changing one after another: first 12 million tomans, then 120 million tomans, then one billion and 200 million tomans, and finally back to 120 million tomans again! A listener who was supposed to learn about the financial problems of a sports discipline probably ended the conversation not so much understanding how much archery costs, but rather wondering: what on earth is going on in sports?!🔸The issue here is not merely a slip of the tongue or a misplaced zero. When the head of a federation—in a discipline where he has been involved for years—cannot give a clear and precise figure for one of the most basic and fundamental costs of the discipline he manages, one has to ask: what has happened to sports management?!🔸It is only natural that the price of specialized equipment varies depending on brand, quality, country of origin, and the athlete's level, and no one expects a federation head to have memorized the price list for every equipment model. But the expectation is that when he speaks with the national media about his discipline's problems, he should at least have a clear, precise, and reliable picture of its main costs.🔸At least once, we need to seriously ask: what has happened to sports that a federation head, in a media interview about one of the most basic issues of the discipline he manages, cannot provide a specific and reliable figure?🔸Of course, the problem is not just Shabani-Bahar; the problem is a structure in which sports managers sometimes have no grasp of the issues in their own discipline—and unfortunately, their number is not small!#نکته_ورزشی #سرویس_ورزشی🔘 بله | ایتا | سروش+ | اینستاگرام | تلگرام@Kayhan_Online

After several…

Source: @Kayhan_online

Deterrent Defense Shield: Negotiation or Counter-Offensive? - 2

After several rounds of failed military operations and the humiliation that followed, the enemy's guard shifted to economic siege and hostility. But unfortunately, some managers, advisers, and analysts still deal with it through the negotiation guard (the catalyst of the enemy's plot).

Certainly, military threats must not be neglected or underestimated. But neither should the enemy's intensified helplessness be forgotten, nor should it be given excessive weight, breeding passivity and fear, and causing neglect of a decisive response to the economic war and siege.

Concern about the enemy's military threat and "treating negotiation as a shelter," even if it had been correct — which it was not — belonged to the stage before the enemy's repeated betrayal of negotiations and imposition of war.

When the war happened, the illusion that negotiation and agreement serve as a deterrent defense shield collapsed. Therefore, one must not again create a bubble for oneself and others and retreat into a shell of passivity; for this behavior amounts to being played by the worn-out tactic of the madman.

The economic siege (maritime and aerial), backed by military action, is a one hundred percent aggressive and criminal military action that must be answered by deploying all kinds of military and non-military threats, symmetrical and asymmetrical.

The enemy has targeted your economy; you too must forcefully strike at its economic interests and Achilles' heels in the commercial and energy domains, the infrastructure related to undersea cables, and... in the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandab, the Indian Ocean, the Sea of Oman, and the Persian Gulf.

This necessary action is precisely the opposite of passive negotiation-seeking, of pressuring the military forces not to bare their claws at America's criminal partners in the region (the UAE and...), and of calming the energy market.

All polls indicate the free fall of Trump's popularity and its clear damage to the position of his political supporters in next month's congressional elections.

The pressure must not be lifted from America. In this regard, the Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council has adopted intelligent and powerful positions, and it is expected that this position will not be weakened by one-sided negotiation signals.

Also, the hands of the operating forces on the ground must be opened wider, and no restrictions or constraints should be created for them.

Not the slightest notion should take shape in the enemy's mind that, in the Iranian side's view, field-oriented actions have subsided and the emphasis and reliance is only on negotiation. This notion is inherently anti-authority and even undermines bargaining power should negotiation become necessary.

💢 Mohammad Imani

🔘 Bale | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram

entry.title:
[Kayhan_online] Deterrent Defense Shield: Negotiation or Counter-Offensive? – 1
When your…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @Kayhan_online

Deterrent Defense Shield: Negotiation or Counter-Offensive? – 1

When your opponent in a contest—a fight—changes stance, you too must change your stance and not remain passive.

America and Israel had clearly come up short in the forty-day war, and the tide had turned, prompting them to seek a ceasefire through intermediaries:

- National unity and cohesion, contrary to the plan for the January overthrow and coup, had been revived and reached its peak.
- The Strait of Hormuz had been closed, humiliating America.
- A significant portion of their offensive and defensive munitions had run out or been strategically depleted.
- Key American bases in the region had been struck. They had nearly been rendered inoperable, yet were still imposing considerable costs on the Pentagon.
- Dozens of fighter jets, helicopters, and drones had been shot down.
- Attempts to reopen the strait or penetrate deep into Iran had failed.
- Iran kept revealing new intelligence and military cards.
- Oil prices during the war had risen to $126.
- And more...

One can accept that, for certain considerations, the Iranian side agreed to a (temporary) ceasefire and would use this time to regroup and reorganize forces, capabilities, and plans.

What is not reasonable was tying the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to the ceasefire.

There was no reason that, while the hostile party had twice betrayed during negotiations and committed great and unprecedented crimes, it should receive a concession on the level of reopening the strait through that strange tweet by Mr. Araghchi.

What was America's reaction? Trump, at the same time as oil prices crashed, announced he would impose a naval blockade against Iran!

This, even though at the height of the war, under pressure from oil prices, he had been forced to suspend some oil sanctions so that Iranian oil could reach the market.

If the justification is an existential threat, Trump later raised this threat more than ten more times. And before that, he never shied away from any crime—unless he was unable to commit it.

Delving into the rest of the story regarding the "memorandum of understanding" is beyond the scope of this analysis.

Whatever judgment we hold about the memorandum of understanding—whether we call it an "honor—a great achievement" or deem it a "mirage/deception operation"—unfortunately, the stance of some of those in charge has not changed after the enemy violated the agreement.

💢To be continued

🔘 Bale | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram

🔰 Instead of making demands of the people, put a stop to cronyism and mismanagement!

🔸Yousef Pezeshkian, the president's son, has written in a note on social media: "You who claim to be at the forefront — lead the way. Live like the people of Yemen: don't take subsidies, don't use the national electricity grid, cut your living costs in half. If these same self-sacrificing people can halve their living costs, then the government too will be able to stand tall against its enemies!"

🔸It is unclear by what authority and on the basis of what experience the president's son is pronouncing on everything and prescribing austerity for the "self-sacrificing nation" — and that, too, in a government that never stops talking about consensus!

🔸These entitled remarks come as the "self-sacrificing" ones are the true symbol of republicanism, resilience, and national authority in the face of enemy threats. A people who for more than 200 days have stood by the country and the revolution with ungrudging steadfastness, despite runaway inflation, and the strategic meaning of their presence is the defense of Iran's territorial integrity.

🔸The key point is that this sacrificing class generally comes from the weaker strata of society: owners of small homes, few or no cars, minimal consumption of water, electricity, and gasoline — those whose entire share of the revolution's table is a meager subsidy of at most 400,000 tomans. These people have been on the streets since the beginning of the war, have endured a hard livelihood, and unlike some managers and officials, have raised no complaints.

🔸The main question for the claimants is this: why does the government's force only reach this class? Why are the massive subsidies of the wealthy — who own dozens of cars and high-consumption villas and are traveling every week — not cut? Why is nothing said about the country's main assets being squandered in banks and state-owned companies, or about astronomical salaries and billion-toman bonuses?

🔸The main problem is not the low costs of the "self-sacrificing" people, but the management model and unnecessary extravagance, luxury per-diem allowances and billion-toman trips, lack of planning, and inefficiency. Riyadh is showing up not as a mere observer but as America's proxy, sharpening its teeth for Iran's gains and lying in wait to seize a pressure lever like the Strait of Hormuz. 🔸The postponement of the Oman meeting at Saudi Arabia's request showed that Riyadh plays a role beyond that of an observer and has become a lever of pressure on the course of the Iran-Oman initiative, having taken a position lying in wait for the meeting's outcome. 🔸Riyadh is trying to steer the meeting's outcome in America's favor; to that end, under the pretext of Yemen's attack on pipelines, it requested the meeting's postponement, which was granted with Oman's agreement.🔸Kayhan newspaper on Sunday, under the headline "Oman safeguards America's interests, the Muscat meeting is a trap, be careful!" warned against this deceptive regional initiative and, raising a question, wrote: "The fundamental and vital question is: at a time when the enemy has hit closed doors on the military battlefield and in the economic war, why should Iran's upper hand and winning card in the Strait of Hormuz be laid on the Muscat table?"🔸Riyadh's presence at this meeting — not merely as an independent country but in the guise of an actor aligned with America's interests — can turn Iran's gains into a "bargaining chip," such that what Iran today holds as a lever and tangible achievement is placed on the negotiating table in exchange for promises and concessions on credit. 🔸Saudi Arabia requested the meeting's postponement under the pretext of Yemen's attack and showed it has the power to influence the course of a diplomatic matter; it is not unlikely that it will show up at the meeting with an American proposal package in order to buy off the pressure lever and battlefield gains on credit with deceptive, unguaranteed promises.#تیتر_یک #سرویس_سیاسی https://kayhan.ir/001PwP🔘 بله | ایتا | سروش+ | اینستاگرام | تلگرام@Kayhan_Online
